s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive gait disturbance with spinal cord compression
salient_findings: Decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
Clonus and hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
Diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1 with near-circumferential epidural extension
key_facts: 1-week history of rapidly progressive gait disturbance
No back pain, fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
No history of smoking or known malignancy
Full strength throughout all extremities
Decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
Four beats of clonus bilaterally
Hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body
No evidence of primary malignancy on CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Laboratory studies, including inflammatory markers, were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with epidural extension

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with spinal cord compression

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solitary expansile bony lesion with spinal cord compression

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with aggressive features

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with aggressive bony lesion

raw.rationale: The expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements, along with the absence of systemic symptoms and no evidence of primary malignancy, is most consistent with a chordoma, which is a rare bone tumor that can cause spinal cord compression and neurological decline.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms such as bone pain, fevers, night sweats, and weight loss, which are absent in this case.

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a solitary lesion and may have systemic symptoms or abnormal laboratory studies, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Less likely to cause severe spinal cord compression and neurological decline, and often has a more gradual onset of symptoms.

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with pain and swelling at the site of the tumor, and is more common in younger patients with a history of prior radiation or Paget's disease.
